analytic_proof: Let D be a convex finite ambient box. Define psi(X)=phi(X)-X. If phi is continuous and piecewise C1 on finite station slabs and sup_D ||Dpsi||2<=L<1, integrate psi along the straight segment joining any X,Y in D. The finite C0 joins preserve the fundamental-theorem bound: |psi(X)-psi(Y)|<=L|X-Y|. Consequently (1-L)|X-Y|<=|phi(X)-phi(Y)|<=(1+L)|X-Y|, proving global one-to-one on D and inverse Lipschitz constant<=1/(1-L) only on phi(D). A line lying in a join plane uses the common nodal rigid-pose tangent; no cross-node C1 assumption is needed.

For a segment of station length h, station s=a dot (X-start), t=(s-s0)/h, chord derivative v=(c1-c0)/h, c(t)=c0+t(c1-c0), u(t)=u0+tDeltaU, w=X-c(t), R(t)=R0 Exp(t[omega]), omega=Log(R0T R1): phi=c+u+Rw and D(phi-I)=(R-I)(I-v aT)+(DeltaU/h+R[omega]w/h)aT. The centerline cancellation is exact; no duplicate (I-R)a term is added.

On each source-supported SO3 shortest-log branch, absolute angles obey theta(t)<=min(theta0+t|omega|,theta1+(1-t)|omega|). Thus Theta<=min(pi,(theta0+theta1+|omega|)/2) bounds every geodesic interpolant; endpoint maximum alone is not generally a bound. ||R-I||2=2sin(theta/2), ||[omega]||2=|omega| and ||b aT||2=|b||a| give Li<=2sin(Theta/2)||I-v aT||2+|a|(|DeltaU|+|omega|Wi)/h.

The arm w(X) is affine for each segment. Every box point is a convex combination of its eight corners, so Wi=max_corner|w| bounds its norm throughout the box, conservatively even outside the segment slab. For an exact straight unit-axis source chart v=a, I-v aT is the cross projector with norm1 and w is the transverse arm. Li then reduces to2sin(Theta/2)+|DeltaU|/h+|omega|*max_cross_radius/h.

The frozen clamped station fractions produce rigid endpoint extensions phi=ci+ui+Ri(X-ci), where ||D(phi-I)||2=2sin(theta_i/2). At every shared station plane both neighboring segment values agree with that same nodal rigid pose, as do the endpoint extensions. They are C0 with one-sided derivative jumps. The maximum of all segment and both endpoint bounds supplies a whole-box Lipschitz bound.

This is a sufficient analytic criterion. L>=1 is inconclusive, not inversion or noninjectivity. Positive pointwise detF alone is insufficient: (exp(x)cos(y),exp(x)sin(y),z) has detF=exp(2x)>0 on a convex box spanning more than2pi in y yet repeats after2pi. This illustrative map is not substituted for the frozen geodesic timber map.
